facts.text: A haul road is the internal road used by trucks in a surface mine or quarry; a berm is a ridge of material piled along an edge as a barrier; a bench is a horizontal step of the pit; and the pit wall is the steep face between benches.
facts.quote: the haul road is the internal road the trucks use, a berm is a ridge of material piled along an edge as a barrier, a bench is one horizontal step of the pit, and the pit wall is the steep face between benches.

facts.text: Surface-mine haul roads run along benches and up ramps, with grades that can exceed 9%.
facts.quote: Haul roads run along benches and up ramps, with grades that can exceed 9% [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Berms along road and dump edges are made of piled earth or rock and are called windrows or bunds in Australia.
facts.quote: Along road and dump edges, crews pile up a ridge of earth or rock called a berm (in Australia a windrow or bund).

facts.text: Berms are intended to stop drifting trucks from going over an edge, and drivers also use dump berms as bump stops.
facts.quote: It is meant to stop a drifting truck going over the edge, and drivers also use the dump berm as a bump stop [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Berms and dump points cause many deaths that are not collisions with people or vehicles: of 54 US haul-truck deaths from 2005 to mid-2021, 21 were berm-related.
facts.quote: These features cause many deaths that are not collisions with people or vehicles: of 54 US haul-truck deaths from 2005 to mid-2021, 21 were berm-related

facts.text: Of 54 US haul-truck deaths from 2005 to mid-2021, 12 occurred at dump points; 10 of those involved an absent or inadequate berm.
facts.quote: of 54 US haul-truck deaths from 2005 to mid-2021, 21 were berm-related and 12 were at dump points, where 10 involved an absent or inadequate berm [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Berms and walls are large, solid, legitimate objects for a sensor.
facts.quote: For a sensor, berms and walls are large, solid, legitimate objects.

facts.text: The NIOSH radar study deliberately excluded berm detections from nuisance detections because driving over a dump edge is deadly.
facts.quote: The NIOSH radar study deliberately did not count berm detections as nuisance, because driving over a dump edge is deadly [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Regulators propose false-activation tests for berms and windrows.
facts.quote: Regulators propose false-activation tests for berms and windrows [Chapter 3].

facts.text: A collision mitigation system that only detects people and vehicles addresses an incomplete part of the fatal-risk picture.
facts.quote: A system that only sees people and vehicles addresses an incomplete part of the fatal-risk picture

facts.text: A collision mitigation system that brakes for every berm would be unusable.
facts.quote: one that brakes for every berm would be unusable [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Virtual sites must locate berms accurately because an edge modeled tens of centimeters out of place can corrupt a stopping-distance test.
facts.quote: Virtual sites must place berms accurately: an edge modeled tens of centimeters out of place can corrupt a stopping-distance test [Chapter 5].
